reasoning: A hybrid strategy combines autonomous pattern recognition with robust XAI tools to detect shared spurious features. Autonomous analysis helps identify obvious commonalities across instances, such as recurring categorical values, while XAI tools provide quantitative attribution scores to validate which features dominate predictions despite lacking semantic relevance. This combination increases both accuracy and confidence in identifying truly spurious correlations.

autonomous_tasks.query: Identify all features that appear in every misclassified instance (13590, 2021, 13302) and note their values across instances.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A list of shared features with their values in each instance, indicating potential shared spurious patterns

autonomous_tasks.query: Evaluate whether any shared feature has a plausible but semantically weak correlation to the target class (income), such as workclass or relationship, despite being non-causal.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A reasoned judgment on whether any shared feature is likely spurious (i.e., not semantically related to income classification)

tool_selection.reasoning: SHAP provides consistent, interpretable feature attributions across instances and identifies which features have high influence despite lack of semantic relevance. LIME offers local explanations to capture model behavior for individual misclassifications. Integrated gradients offer smooth, baseline-aware attribution, helping detect spurious patterns across the input space. Sensitivity analysis quantifies how much prediction changes when specific features are removed, confirming spurious dependencies. Together, these tools validate the autonomous findings with robust, model-agnostic evidence.
